sections.overview: Elops senegalensis is a West African ladyfish in genus Elops and a close relative of E. lacerta.
sections.identification: It has 11–15 lower-arch gill rakers and 92–100 lateral-line scales, unlike E. lacerta.
sections.habitat: It inhabits eastern Atlantic coastal waters from Mauritania south to the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
sections.diet: Its recorded prey include fish and shrimps.
sections.behavior: This coastal pelagic fish occurs inshore and can move up tidal rivers.
sections.reproduction: The regional guide reports spawning at sea and a transparent leptocephalus larval stage for coastal Elops.
sections.ecology: It overlaps with E. lacerta in West African coastal food webs; E. machnata is a related Indo-West Pacific species.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports the global IUCN category Data Deficient, assessed in 2019.
